steps.text: My words don't matter much. Only when you live free, in every moment, are you truly alive.
Go and experience the world for yourself. It will take many months to form your own ideas.
Kal'tsit, I hope you will...
5:39 P.M. \ Clear
Outdoors, Rhodes Island Deck

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You've been quite busy lately, right? There are many things you have to do.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Proper rest is also necessary. There have been some small fluctuations in your psychological indicators as of late, and I will continue to monitor them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Right, Blaze will be here to give you a report tonight. She was the one who led the raid yesterday.
1:23 A.M. \ Rainy
Babel Temporary Operational Command Center

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Scout's outside, he was in charge of last night's operation.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is the record of one of his rare mission failures since enlisting in Babel.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Come in.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Commander, Dame, you're both here. Let me briefly explain what happened last night.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: When my squad was sweeping the battlefield, they found traces of enemy troops that could be tracked. I made the decision that this was an opportunity to sniff out the enemy's position, insisted on giving chase, and ended up being ambushed.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: The responsibility is mine alone, and I am willing to accept the army's punishment.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: This is not a decision an old Sarkaz mercenary would make.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Regrettably, all my experience failed to let me know anything was wrong.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Something has to actually happen for your experience to be worth anything. You lost no team members after the crisis occurred, indicating that your command was calm as you retreated, and thus proper.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: You deserve recognition, not punishment.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I don't understand how you reached this conclusion.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Army discipline loses all meaning if it fails to recognize when to reward and when to punish. You know that, Scout.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Why do you care so much about her reputation? I need a reason.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Dame Kal'tsit, how's Reyka?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She's out of danger.
Scout opens his mouth to say something, but words fail him.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Your heart is in turmoil. Rarely have I seen you struggle like this, even on the battlefield. If you can tell us what you're thinking, maybe we can...

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I insist that Reyka not be punished in any way.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Because she's an orphan? Military discipline isn't a bleeding heart operation.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Reyka's father was a Sarkaz mercenary who died in the civil war.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: She's in good company in Kazdel.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Her mother suffered from severe Oripathy and was unable to raise her. Upon learning about this, Her Majesty Theresa has been providing financial support to their family.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Nothing special about that either. If you don't have any better reason...

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: Reyka only enlisted in the army to repay Her Majesty's kindness.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: She once told me that fighting for Her Majesty is her only wish and the entire purpose of her life...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Go on, Scout. I'm listening.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: In Kazdel, it is rare for children to have any wishes, or anything to protect.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: They get sucked into the maelstrom of war, and then they die.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: So you hope to preserve Reyka's reputation, to keep her wish to protect Her Majesty alive.
Scout cannot answer, the battle-tested veteran falls back into silence.
The Doctor rises slowly, reaching out to pat Scout on the shoulder. Kal'tsit does not expect this.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Sorry if that offended you. I knew you must've had a good reason.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: No one will be punished. But that will have an impact on discipline, which isn't going to be popular.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Scout, I hope that in the future, you and your team will respond to doubt with action.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I swear to do this. Commander, Dame, I'll be taking my leave.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Promise me one thing before you go. Value your own life and reputation the same as you do your teammates.

steps.name: Scout
steps.text: I will.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Additionally... Closure may approach you to discuss the Londinium issue. She's very concerned about my position on this matter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You can share some more of the decision-making process with her. After all, she is also a potential combat operator.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Of course, you can also discuss... other things.
11:27 A.M. \ Clear
Rhodes Island Chief Engineer's Office

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What is it this time?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm wondering if you've settled on the going-to-Londinium thing?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm still discussing it, as the action itself is rather risky. Why are you suddenly so concerned about this?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I'm worried you're not in the right headspace. I know you want to go, deep down, but you gotta think about the kind of danger we're up against.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You waste a lot of energy getting all torn up.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm not torn up. Rhodes Island's safety is always my first priority.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It'd be great if one day, you could just do whatever you want.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: You can't put it past me. I know how close you are to Theresa. There's no way you can stay out of the Londinium thingy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This has nothing to do with Her Majesty. I only care about the pros and cons that the action itself has on Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah yeah, I know, always responsibility and duty. Take a day to treat yourself every once in a while.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Leave all the boring stuff to the Doctor, and let's knock some back, just the two of us. Doesn't that sound nice?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Doctor is already working very hard.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I guess that's true. You'd think the amnesia would give us an all new Doctor, but the workaholic part is still the same.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But honestly, the old Doctor was such a hardass, I like the new version better.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Because this one's easier to bully?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I heard about the treadmill you gave the Doctor, how it would start floating for no reason, and you had to watch ads to get it back down.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That was a special promotion! I was trying to save the Doctor money.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I need you to be more considerate. The last thing I need is an overwhelmed Doctor getting scared to death by levitating exercise equipment.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah, sure. Why so serious all of a sudden?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Maybe it's something about how I knew the old Doctor, but I keep getting this uncontrollable urge to pull the most hilarious pranks.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Especially before, when the Doctor was acting weirder and weirder...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Enough, Closure. No more on this subject. I forbid you from mentioning a word of this to the Doctor.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm not that clueless. By the way, Kal'tsit, before we go to Londinium, I'm going to carry out a renovation of the 'under-development area.' Gotta thicken that hull, at least.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: It'll be pricey, but I, a reliable engineer that I am, think that level of investment is still absolutely necessary.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So, on behalf of the Engineering Department, I've decided to fight for three days and nights to give the 'under-development area' a brand new look!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No need. The 'under-development area' is the sturdiest place on the ship.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hehe, I thought you'd say that. Right below the 'under-development area' is a drone hangar, and that hangar doesn't have any support pillars.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Once we knock out the upper part, the top of the hangar will deform, and then...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Kal'tsit, why are you glaring at me like that? I'm scared!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You just want to do your own thing.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Alright, cards on the table. I'm the chief engineer, of course I'm gonna be curious about some place I can't get into.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have my reasons.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: All those secrets in your gullet are gonna suffocate you.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: When are you going to open up to me already? You can't carry this all by yourself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Maybe... that day will come.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Looking forward to it.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait, huh? Did you just say something not super uptight?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The patient placement work for Connor County will be completed today. In the coming days, you'll once again need to reassess the defensive strength of the settlement site.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Medical Department will forward the relevant data to you later.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In the future, similar tasks will gradually be transferred over to elite operators so that your energy will not be diverted from more important issues.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Sorry to barge in, but look alive, everyone. Dr. Kal'tsit is about to start her daily rounds.

steps.name: Ordinary Infected A
steps.text: She's earlier than usual today, huh... Eh? There's a bunch of logistics department folks as well.

steps.name: Ordinary Infected B
steps.text: You should go see Dr. Kal'tsit about that forgetfulness of yours.

steps.name: Ordinary Infected B
steps.text: That lass from the Medical Department came over to our ward for a week or so to touch bases, and said that she was going to transfer all of us to a temporary medical settlement in Connor County. What's the point of other people talking if you're not gonna remember a word of it?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Haha, don't worry, sir. After all, the arrangement was made rather hastily.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I'll be reminding everyone again, the Rhodes Island landship will be conducting a series of mock exercises around Victoria in the near future.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: We've decided to temporarily transfer you to a medical settlement in Connor County out of consideration for your safety.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Please rest assured that the medical facilities there are comprehensive, and you will be accompanied by most of the medical staff.

steps.name: Ordinary Infected A
steps.text: Look, now that's Ari—

steps.name: Ordinary Infected A
steps.text: Gaaaah, Dr. Kal'tsit! How long have you been standing right next to me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Don't worry. I just got here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ari, pass me this patient's blood works report.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Hmm, you've recovered quickly and your Oripathy hasn't shown any signs of deterioration.

steps.name: Ordinary Infected A
steps.text: The fact that I'm still here today is all thanks to you. When I think back to the day I first had an acute Oripathy attack, you didn't close your eyes day or night so you could rescue me. I just...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's my duty as a doctor.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Next, I'll have to read the relevant agreement on the transfer and resettlement, and you'll sign the agreement after I read it. According to Article 4 of Rhodes Island's Oripathy and Treatment Regulations...

steps.name: Ordinary Infected A
steps.text: Easy there, Doctor, you don't have to read all that. Rhodes Island has my complete and total trust, so just show me where I have to sign.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I appreciate it, but reading out the agreement in its entirety is also to protect your rights.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Ari, time is short, and we might not have the manpower to carry the patients. Check the hallway to see if anyone can help.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Ah, Doctor? Good afternoon, what brings you here?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Doctor, are you available right now? We don't have enough staff to relocate the patients here, and might need your help...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Given your current physical condition, I'd recommend you not engage in any physical labor.

options: I've got nothing better to do.
At least let me give it a shot! Don't underestimate me!

steps.name: Ordinary Infected B
steps.text: Doctor... This isn't the commander of Rhodes Island, is it? The one that Little Ari's always talking about every day?

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: S-Sir, please don't say silly things like that! Doctor, I was just giving them an overview of Rhodes Island.

options: She's probably giving me too much credit.

steps.name: Ordinary Infected A
steps.text: Having the commander of Rhodes Island transport me? There's no way...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now don't be shy. Everyone in Rhodes Island is obligated to help in even the most commonplace of tasks. That hardly changes even for the person with the title of field commander.

options: Our time is limited. Let's get the transfer underway.
Qus, come here and help me lift his upper body, and pay attention to the medical equipment cable.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Sure thing. Ari, what's this new device? Never seen it before.

options: It's a crystal melting instrument, Rhine Lab CR-01 experimental model, with a built-in Originium circuit.
In the middle and late stages of Oripathy, the body becomes filled with crystals, and the organs are easily damaged and ruptured.
The crystal melting instrument utilizes the sequential release of concentrated energy to dissolve the crystallization.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: That's exactly right! See, it's just as I said, the Doctor really knows everything.

options: Qus, don't just lift like that.
Use your left hand to place the patient's hands together over the side of your neck, then use your right hand to cradle both the patient's legs...

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: S-Sorry...! I didn't pay very close attention to Dr. Kal'tsit's battlefield handling course, and didn't learn a lot of that material...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That course was originally structured for you to cement your knowledge with practice anyway. But how did you know that, Doctor? If I recall, you were out in Sargon during that session.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: One last thing, Amiya's been busy with various assessments of the Londinium trip as of late. Please take the time to make sure you look after her.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She may be the leader of Rhodes Island, but she is also still a kid.
2:29 A.M. \ Overcast
Babel Temporary Operational Command Center

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are the leader of Babel, but you're also an Oripathy patient. Please take your health seriously.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I suggest you stop working and take a break immediately.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Kal'tsit, you still think too much about others... Oh, Doctor, please come in. We weren't discussing anything confidential.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: I heard everything, Your Majesty. You really should be getting enough sleep.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: That was a tense meeting we had last night. All that battle talk must have tired you out.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No worries. Conversely, Doctor, I would like to apologize for the words spoken by some of the participants. They did not intend to offend, but were slightly agitated.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: They were worried about my safety, but I understand that you must surely have considered all possible situations. This is the best solution.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Theresis wants to regain the initiative. He knows that your strengths are also your weaknesses.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: But what he doesn't know is how much you're willing to sacrifice for the Sarkaz people.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: When Ascalon's troops arrive in town, he'll see the writing on the wall.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're always so reassuring. Doctor, listening to your words is more refreshing than sleeping.
Theresa's weary face flashes a smile of relief, a smile that becomes gentler as she looks out the door.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Come in. Here, sit next to me.

steps.name: Small Cautus
steps.text: B-But...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No need to look all around. There are no outsiders here, Amiya.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, Dr. Kal'tsit, g-good evening.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I didn't mean to stay up this late.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No one is blaming you, dear. Let me guess, did you have a nightmare?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No... I didn't. The soldiers moving around woke me up.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I was looked out the window and saw Ascalon getting ready for a long trip with the other fighters...

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: They are on a mission.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But... But, Ascalon said she would never leave me or Her Majesty.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I was worried, so I snuck in here to take a look...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Amiya, my dear Amiya, the Doctor gave Ascalon a little job. They'll be back soon enough.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Think about it, has one of the Doctor's battles ever run long?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Y-You're right.. If that's what Doctor wants, I feel much better.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor is the best at making everyone feel safe.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Amiya, you should rest.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Okay I'm going to bed! Good night, everyone!

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What a sweet, lovable child...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, before you came, I was a bit worried... about the safety of the Rhodes Island landship in Ascalon's absence.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: That's natural.

steps.name: Doctor
steps.text: Stretching his front line thin, encircling a small town with no strategic significance. There's no telling what Theresis's true objective is.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: My safety is secondary. I'm more concerned about the safety of the children and researchers on the ship.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But as Amiya said, you really do give people a sense of security. What you've accomplished through your command leaves no room for doubt.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Doctor, Kal'tsit, the day we win this war... shouldn't be far away, right?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now, all of that is well outside your normal schedule...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, are you still listening?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, what does it mean to be truly alive?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Obeying someone else's will, losing your reason to move on. Does that count as being alive?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Keeping your body, but being separated from your memories. Does that count as being alive?

options: That might make life rather confusing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you had to choose one or the other, Doctor, which would you choose?

options: I choose to be human, not a puppet.
I would choose to be free.
Who wants to be a robot?

a.text: Kal'tsit casts a deeply pensive look at you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Freedom is not free.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: After you lost your memories, you woke up, were forced to fight, and forced to witness the sacrifice of human life. This whole time, you have barely had a single choice...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Look into my eyes... Tell me, Doctor, why is it that you fight?

a.text: Memories continue to pour forth in this moment, and everything that has happened since your awakening in Chernobog flashes before your eyes vividly, joy and sorrow intertwining.
An answer becomes clearer and clearer in your mind. You almost blurt it out subconsciously—

options: I am fighting against my destiny.
I fight to protect this world.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Make sure you don't forget the answer you just gave me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even if no one understands, we must continue to walk this path.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, you too will find your path.
